objectives: This study assessed the safety and effectiveness of mpox and historical smallpox vaccines administered during pregnancy and childhood.
inclusion_criteria: The manuscript's explicit eligibility section states that the review planned to include randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, cohort studies, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, case series, and case reports (only for novel adverse events) assessing the safety (any outcome) and efficacy/effectiveness (infections, hospitalizations, and disease-related death) of any vaccinia-based vaccines administered to children, adolescents, and pregnant persons. Neonates were defined as birth to 28 days, children as older than 28 days and younger than 12 years, adolescents as 12-17 years, and pediatric as the umbrella category for all individuals younger than 18 years. Interventions of interest included mpox and historical smallpox vaccines regardless of generation; comparators could be active or inactive interventions not under evaluation, standard care, or placebo; non-comparative study designs were eligible. Table 2 also shows that immunogenicity outcomes were extracted/reported for some included studies.
exclusion_criteria: No standalone exclusion subsection was provided. Based on the inverse of the inclusion criteria plus Table S2, excluded records were those with the wrong intervention, wrong outcomes, wrong study design, wrong population (for example immunogenicity-only studies with n<10), duplicate reports, trial-registry records with no posted results or whose results were already available in a publication, and studies outside the target maternal/pediatric populations. The manuscript also states that adult-population results will be reported separately.

selection_evidence: Results state that 27 clinical studies were included (19 in pregnant persons and 8 in children/adolescents). Main-manuscript Table 2 lists the 19 maternal studies and, across its continued pediatric section, the 8 pediatric studies. Table S6 in the supplement confirms the pediatric eight by name: Decker 2021, Duffy 2024, Ladhani 2023, Lane 1970a, Lane 1970b, Muller 2024, Sharff 2023, and Yamaguchi 1975. The included studies therefore come from main Table 2, cross-checked against the Results count and supplemental risk-of-bias tables.
notes:
Fell back to study_entries because a complete literature-only ref-number list is not possible: one included pediatric study, Yamaguchi 1975, is cited in main Table 2 as ref [68], but ref [68] in the manuscript is a Google Scholar URL rather than a literature citation. Exclusion criteria were synthesized from the explicit inclusion section plus Table S2 because the paper does not provide a separate exclusion-criteria subsection. The PubMed query was reconstructed from Table S1; the OCR text for PubMed set #64 appears inconsistent, and the final logic was aligned with the parallel EMBASE/CINAHL strategies.
